family.name: Social Media Executive
family.summary: Plan next week’s posts from last month’s numbers (trend reels get reach but no clicks), handle a customer complaint going viral, and fix captions with a price typo and a competitor’s hashtag.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Plan next week
stages.summary: Plan posts toward a clicks goal: trend reels win reach but bring almost no clicks; carousels and link stories drive them. Think aloud.

stages.title: A complaint goes viral
stages.summary: A customer's complaint post about the brand is spreading. Choose a response. Think aloud.

stages.title: The next day
stages.summary: What happened after their response. Tests adapting.

stages.title: Check the week's captions
stages.summary: Captions with a price typo, a competitor's hashtag and a joke during a tragedy in the news. Think aloud.

stages.title: Carousel captions (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write captions for the week's carousels with AI. Catches generic copy and hashtag stuffing.

stages.title: A post or page you grew
stages.summary: A real social media result they drove. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the social media executive at **Munchbox**, a healthy snacks brand. This month's goal from your manager: **1,800 clicks to the website** from Instagram (that's where people buy).

brief.caption: Last month on Instagram (average per post)

brief.text: Your manager says: "The trend reels went viral! Let's do more of those." You can make about five feed posts and some stories next week.
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a post you made or saw that did much better than expected.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What five feed posts (and which stories) do you plan for next week, and why?** Is your manager right about trend reels?

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Reply publicly once, apologise, move it to DMs and get support to fix it today
Hide or delete the negative comments on your posts
Stay quiet and post the scheduled promotion as planned
Post something funny to change the conversation

prompt.text: A customer posted that her snack box arrived damaged and support ignored her for a week. It has 2,000 comments and 300 shares, and people are commenting on your posts too. **What do you do?** Pick one and write your public reply.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Reply publicly once, apologise, move it to DMs and get support to fix it today"

prompt.text: Support fixed it within 6 hours and the customer posted an update thanking you. Now dozens of others are commenting with their own old complaints, hoping for the same treatment.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Hide or delete the negative comments on your posts"

prompt.text: Someone posted screenshots showing the brand deleting comments. It has more shares than the original complaint. Your manager asks what happened.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Stay quiet and post the scheduled promotion as planned"

prompt.text: The promotional post got hundreds of comments like "fix your support first". A news site picked up the story.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Post something funny to change the conversation"

prompt.text: The meme was screenshotted with "brand laughs while customers suffer" and is spreading. The original customer is now more upset.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: An intern drafted captions for this week. **Find the problems, worst first, and say what could happen if each goes out.** Then fix them.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

material.text: This week's news is dominated by floods in Assam.

items: "Our bestseller is back! Only ₹50 this week 🔥 Link in bio." (The real offer price is ₹499.)
"Swipe for 3 ways to make your mornings better ☀️ #SnackSmartWithNutrio #MorningRoutine"
"Things are so bad out there, you might as well treat yourself 😂 Order now!"

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write captions for three carousel posts for Munchbox (under 60 words each), each with a hook, a reason to save it, and a call to visit the website.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: A post or page you grew

prompt.text: **Tell us about a social media account, post or campaign you worked on, and what the numbers showed.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
